Container.Name: Audiobind
Container.Overview: Finds audiobooks that are split into many files, checks each one against the Audible catalog, merges the parts into a single tagged m4b with real chapter marks and cover art, and files it as Author/Book/Book.m4b (or Author/Series/3 - Title/). Runs on a timer and only converts books it is confident about. Optional: a wishlist that searches your private tracker and hands finds to qBittorrent, Deluge, Transmission or rTorrent, then converts what lands.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: audiobook m4b merge convert chapters metadata audible audnex audiobookshelf wishlist tracker qbittorrent

Set Max runtime delta to 0.15 by hand, and if you never set qBittorrent URL, set it now. * Setup can now be checked instead of guessed: Check IP shows the address the tracker would see, Test tracker runs a real search and reports what it found, Test qBittorrent names the categories and the save path, and a preset file can fill the tracker fields or supply the category list. ### 0.25.0 * Wishlist: saving a search title no longer re-queues the book, so retitling one mid-download can no longer grab a second torrent. A new Re-queue button is the deliberate way back. * A disk that stops answering ffprobe now fails the book instead of converting it with chapters missing. * Fixed: a malformed detail row took the whole status page down with a 500. * Much faster status polling and page renders (covering indexes; the poll is about fifty times cheaper at 3,000 books). ### 0.24.0 * A fresh install answers on private LAN addresses out of the box: Allowed hosts can be left blank. * Set Allowed hosts to a list to restrict the UI to exactly those names (DNS-rebinding guard). ### 0.23.0 * Settings > Watcher > Allowed-IP updater: keeps the tracker's dynamic seedbox IP in step with your VPN, off/notify/auto, at most once an hour * Settings > Library > Hardcover: a second opinion on series and position in a book's detail panel. Container.Description:
### What it does
Point Audiobind at a folder of audiobooks and a folder to write to. On a timer it:
1. **Groups parts into books** - `Book/Disc 1`, `Book/Part 2` and `Book/Part 10` become one book, not three. 2. **Verifies the book** against the Audible catalog: title, author, narrator, series, ASIN. 3. **Proves completeness** by comparing total runtime with the catalog runtime. A set that is an hour short is reported, not merged. 4. **Merges and converts**: one `.m4b`, AAC stereo at a 128 kbps floor (a richer source keeps its own bitrate; `AUDIO_CHANNELS=1` halves the file size), real chapter marks from Audnex, cover art and full tags embedded. 5. **Files it** as `Author/Book/Book.m4b` (or `Author/Series/3 - Title/Title.m4b`), with an Audiobookshelf-compatible `metadata.json`. Every author is in the folder, joined with ` & `.
### What it will not do
* Conversion never changes, moves or deletes your source files. Only the explicit Delete button in the web UI can remove a source folder (a confirmation dialog, no undo), and only while the library is mounted writable; set the library path to Read Only to rule even that out. * It does not convert anything it is unsure about. Matches that are only partial, or whose runtime disagrees with the catalog by more than 15%, are marked **review**/**held** on the status page for you to look at.
Suitable for Audiobookshelf, Plex, Emby, Jellyfin, Apple Books and anything else that reads standard m4b chapters and tags.

Config.Name: Library path
Config.Description: Folder holding the audiobooks to fix. Writable so Delete can fully remove a book. Owner decides: set Access Mode to Read Only for a guarantee the app never touches your sources - this disables source-delete (Delete then removes only the output).

Config.Name: Output path
Config.Description: Where finished m4b files are written. Never the same as the library path.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Database, audit report and work files.

Config.Name: WebUI port
Config.Description: Status page and JSON API. Change it if another container already uses this port.

Config.Name: Web port (inside the container)
Config.Description: Leave at 8080. Change it only if Audiobind runs inside a VPN container's network and another app there (often qBittorrent) already uses 8080: pick another port such as 8686 and publish that port on the VPN container. On the normal bridge network, changing it breaks the WebUI port mapping above.

Config.Name: Allowed hosts
Config.Description: Optional. When this variable is not set at all, the UI answers on this machine and on private LAN addresses (like 192.168.1.10), but not on hostnames. Any value here restricts it: set a comma-separated list of the names/IPs you open the web UI with, e.g. 192.168.1.10,tower,tower.local: then only exactly those are answered (protects against DNS-rebinding attacks).

Config.Name: Access token
Config.Description: Only for upgrading: an install that still signs in with a token keeps working while this is set. On a new install leave it empty and create your account on the setup page that opens on the first visit. It asks for the one-time setup code printed in the container log on the first start (look for 'setup code'). Scripts send it as 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN'.

Config.Name: Trusted proxy
Config.Description: true only when Audiobind sits behind your own reverse proxy: X-Forwarded-Host/-For/-Proto from the addresses in Trusted proxy IPs are then believed. Needs Trusted proxy IPs as well.

Config.Name: Trusted proxy IPs
Config.Description: Comma-separated addresses or CIDRs of your reverse proxy (for example 172.18.0.0/16). Forwarded headers are only honoured from these peers; empty means none.

Config.Name: Auto convert
Config.Description: Which confidence tiers convert without asking: high, medium or off. high converts the books it is sure of on the first scan, which starts as soon as the container does. Choose off to review every match first, then switch to high under Settings.

Config.Name: Scan interval (minutes)
Config.Description: How often to look for new books.

Config.Name: Audio bitrate (floor)
Config.Description: Minimum AAC bitrate. A richer source keeps its own bitrate (a 256k mp3 stays 256k); anything below this is lifted to it. Capped at 320k.

Config.Name: Channels
Config.Description: 1 = mono, 2 = stereo. Stereo keeps the source layout; mono halves the file size.

Config.Name: Parallel jobs
Config.Description: Books converted at once. Raise if your CPU is idle.

Config.Name: Nice level
Config.Description: CPU priority for ffmpeg. Higher = yields to everything else.

Config.Name: Max runtime delta
Config.Description: Hold a book when its runtime differs from the catalog by more than this fraction (0.15 = 15%).

Config.Name: Region
Config.Description: Audible region for metadata: us, uk, ca, au, de.

Config.Name: Dry run
Config.Description: true = log every decision but write nothing.

Config.Name: Log file
Config.Description: Path of the rotating log file (5 MB, 3 backups). Written next to the console log, so it survives a container recreate. Set it to empty only if you want no file log.

Config.Name: Notify URL
Config.Description: Optional webhook (Discord/Slack/ntfy) posted a summary after each scan.

Config.Name: Ingest path
Config.Description: Optional. Folder where downloaded audiobooks land (for example qBittorrent's completed folder for the wishlist watcher). Mounted read-only. Leave empty to turn ingest off.

Config.Name: Ingest dir
Config.Description: Set to /ingest when the Ingest path above is used; empty = ingest off.

Config.Name: Tracker URL
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Needed for the wishlist. Base URL of your private tracker, e.g. https://tracker.example (no path). A path here (e.g. a pasted bookmark) stops the container from starting. The wishlist watcher is off until this, both paths, the search body, the cookie name and the session are set (plus the qBittorrent address and login below).

Config.Name: Tracker search path
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Needed for the wishlist. Path of the tracker's JSON search endpoint.

Config.Name: Tracker search method
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Optional. POST (default) or GET.

Config.Name: Tracker search category
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Optional. The category value to send with a search, if the site needs one. Empty = none is sent.

Config.Name: Tracker search encoding
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Optional. How a POST sends the search body: json (default) or form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded key=value pairs).

Config.Name: Tracker search body
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Needed for the wishlist. The search request as a JSON object with {{title}}, {{author}} and {{category}} placeholders, e.g. {"q": "{{title}} {{author}}"}. A member that is only placeholders and comes out empty is left out. A value here that is not a JSON object stops the container from starting.

Config.Name: Tracker download path
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Needed for the wishlist. Path of the tracker's torrent download endpoint.

Config.Name: Tracker download id field
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Optional. Query parameter carrying the torrent id (default tid).

Config.Name: Tracker freeleech field
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Optional. Query parameter that spends a freeleech credit, e.g. fl. Empty = never sent.

Config.Name: Tracker cookie name
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Needed for the wishlist. The name of the tracker's session cookie.

Config.Name: Tracker session (secret)
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Needed for the wishlist. The value of the tracker's session cookie. Create the session for the IP the container reaches the tracker from. A secret.

Config.Name: Tracker proxy
Config.Description: Optional. http://host:port (or https://) proxy for every tracker request, e.g. a VPN container's HTTP proxy. Empty = direct. Fail-closed: a dead proxy means no tracker request, never a direct one. This covers Audiobind's own visits to the tracker (searches and .torrent files). The download itself is qBittorrent's; route qBittorrent through your VPN separately. Prefer running Audiobind in the VPN container's network (see Running the watcher through a VPN: https://github.com/stinger303/audiobind/blob/main/docs/acquisition.md#running-the-watcher-through-a-vpn).

Config.Name: Tracker user agent
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Optional. Text to send as the User-Agent to the tracker. Empty = audiobind/<version>. Set to none to send no User-Agent (some trackers refuse that with HTTP 400).

Config.Name: Tracker VIP / Premium member
Config.Description: Easier: fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Set to true if your account holds the tracker's top membership tier (some trackers call it VIP, others Premium). When false, torrents restricted to that tier are skipped instead of attempted.

Config.Name: Expected egress IP (guard)
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). Optional. Your VPN's exit address. When set, the watcher checks which IP the tracker would see before every cycle and refuses to contact it unless it is exactly this one. Leave empty to skip this check.

Config.Name: Home IP (guard)
Config.Description: Optional. Your home connection's public IP. When set, the watcher checks which IP the tracker would see before every cycle and refuses to contact it if it is this one, or if it cannot tell. One small HTTPS request per cycle to ipinfo.io.

Config.Name: Watcher dry run
Config.Description: true = the watcher searches and logs what it would download, but never downloads. Separate from Dry run.

Config.Name: Watch interval (minutes)
Config.Description: Minutes between wishlist watcher cycles (10-1440).

Config.Name: Watch max per cycle
Config.Description: Wanted books the watcher searches per cycle (1-20). Also editable in Settings > Watcher.

Config.Name: Watch max incomplete
Config.Description: No torrent is added in a cycle while this many in the qBittorrent category are still downloading. 0 = no limit.

Config.Name: qBittorrent URL
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). The address you open qBittorrent's WebUI with, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8080. Only if Audiobind shares a VPN container's network with qBittorrent: http://127.0.0.1:<its port>.

Config.Name: qBittorrent category
Config.Description: Easier: fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). The qBittorrent category torrents are added to. One folder, three names. Example: host folder /mnt/user/downloads/audiobooks → Audiobind's Ingest path (Audiobind calls it /ingest) → in qBittorrent, the category's save path is whatever qBittorrent's own Docker page maps that host folder to (often /downloads/audiobooks or /data/audiobooks). Never type /ingest into qBittorrent.

Config.Name: qBittorrent user
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). qBittorrent WebUI username. The watcher stays disabled without a login.

Config.Name: qBittorrent password
Config.Description: Easier: leave empty and fill this in under Settings > Watcher in the web UI (checked there, no restart). qBittorrent WebUI password.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID for written files.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID for written files.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone for log timestamps.
